summary.title: Python Recommender Systems: Content Based & Collaborative Filtering Recommendation Engines
summary.one_liner: You learn the three main recommender types (simple, content-based, collaborative filtering) and how to build a weighted-rating top-movies chart and a TF-IDF plot-similarity recommender in Python with pandas and scikit-learn.
keywords: how to build a movie recommender
takeaways: Simple recommenders rank items by a score; a weighted rating (IMDB formula) balances average rating against vote count.
Content-based recommenders use item metadata such as plot overviews, and TF-IDF vectors with cosine similarity can find movies with similar plots.
Plot-only content recommendation has limits: it returned all Batman films for The Dark Knight Rises, motivating richer metadata like cast, director and genres.
Collaborative filtering predicts a user's preference from other users' ratings and does not need item metadata.
summary.summary: The tutorial introduces three recommender types and walks through building them on the MovieLens-based metadata dataset (about 45,000 movies). It first builds a simplified IMDB Top 250 clone by computing IMDB's weighted rating, with the vote-count cutoff m set at the 90th percentile. It then builds a plot-description recommender by computing TF-IDF vectors with scikit-learn, comparing movies with linear_kernel cosine similarity, and returning the ten closest titles. The page ends by noting the plot-only results are weak and introducing a next section on credits, genres and keywords; the collaborative filtering part is described conceptually rather than implemented in the text shown.
